notes.9: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. This suggests that some candidates assumed that two MnO 2– ions give one MnO – ion and one MnO formula unit. However this is a redox reaction. MnO 2– to 4 4 2 4 MnO – involves the loss of one electron while MnO 2– to MnO effectively involves the gain of two electrons 4 4 2 9701 Chemistry June 2017 as the oxidation number of Mn decreases from 6 to 4. In order to balance the electrons involved, three MnO 2– ions give two MnO – ions and one MnO formula unit. 4 4 2
notes.20: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. C, pentan-3-one, would be reduced to pentan-3-ol. This will dehydrate to give cis and trans pent-2-ene; two isomers. B, butanone, would be reduced to butan-2-ol. This will dehydrate to give cis and trans but-2-ene and but-1-ene, three isomers.
notes.28: Many candidates incorrectly gave B as their answer. The answer B is obtained by 2.3×0.6=1.38. This does not take into account the different M values of the reactant and the product. Using an excess of oxidising agent and boiling under reflux for one hour would only be done if the carboxylic acid is the required product. 2.3 g is 0.05 moles of ethanol. The answer is C as the required product is ethanoic acid, since 0.05×60×0.6=1.8.
notes.32: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. The choice of A requires statement 3 to be true, and C cannot be described as ‘giant molecular’. Since C has pentagons of carbon atoms in its structure 60 60 statement 2 is also untrue. Only statement 1 is true, every carbon atom in graphene, graphite and C has an electron in a p-orbital giving rise to delocalised electrons.
notes.33: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. For the majority of candidates statement 2 was the key to this question. An enthalpy change of combustion is defined as the energy change when complete combustion takes place and the equation in the question involves incomplete combustion, so statement 2 is false.
notes.38: The three incorrect choices each attracted approximately equal numbers of candidates, suggesting many candidates may have guessed. Statement 1 is true because a primary halogenoalkane reacts mainly by an S 2 mechanism. Statement 2 is false. The carbon atom in (CH ) CCl will be less positive, not more positive, N 3 3 due to the inductive effect of three alkyl groups. Statement 3 is false, as it is a carbon atom not the chlorine atom that is attacked.
